gaps: The pre-rename recovery instruction does not identify an exact last compatible harness commit or a runnable way to obtain and use it. A developer must guess which version to run, despite the spec making this a prerequisite (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:27; docs/decisions/0088-simple-upgrade.md:39).

The vendored-commit check establishes only that the object exists. The spec does not say whether it must be an ancestor of the harness HEAD, or what happens when the client records a newer commit; proceeding could downgrade the client while presenting the operation as an upgrade (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:24; factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:608).

The worktree scan has no stated fail-closed rule for unreadable or stale Git worktree bookkeeping. The existing worktree enumerator silently skips unreadable entries, so a worktree with in-progress work could be omitted despite the promised refusal (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:31; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:5307).

The work-in-progress definition covers approved active plans but leaves a saved plan awaiting approval with no story pointer unspecified. Archiving its grill or approval files while retaining the plan could strand that handoff; the plan metadata and approval state are separate from the pointer (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:35; factory/scripts/forge_cli/plans.py:82; factory/scripts/forge_cli/plans.py:274).

Parking does not define how every linked worktree's branch and git-local run, stage, and task state is retired. Changing the target branch's roadmap and archive alone leaves a parked task worktree able to continue from its old branch and state (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:42; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:5323; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:163).

Parking moves the plan but does not specify resetting its protected plan metadata or the worktree run pointer. An approved `plan-meta.json` still blocks a new plan save, so returning the roadmap item to pending does not by itself make replanning reachable (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:42; factory/scripts/forge_cli/plans.py:274; factory/scripts/intake.py:76).

The archive table says `grills/` and grill-round files without distinguishing obsolete files from current digest-bound grill records. The board still reads story grill records at that path; archiving them wholesale can erase current handoff evidence from the live readers (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:51; factory/scripts/forge_cli/board.py:905).

The byte-equality ownership rule does not specify how client-added files under the vendored gate trees are handled. Keeping an unknown `factory/scripts` file while regenerating the manifest would freeze client code as gate machinery; the current integrity checker includes every file in those trees (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:57; docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:60; factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46).

The spec promises no writes on refusal but does not define whether acquiring the existing git-local exclusion lock counts or how preflight is ordered around it. The current upgrade acquires that lock before its deeper preflight, so this guarantee needs a precise boundary and test (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:21; factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4613).

The transactional health step omits `forge doctor --fast` and board-data loading even though the first acceptance criterion requires both after success. A commit could be published before either downstream reader is exercised (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:63; docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:94).

The proposed PR-ticket exemption lacks a provenance rule for archive, `.gitignore`, and `.codex` changes. The existing exemption accepts a manifest marker plus allowed path names, so extending those names alone could exempt a hand-authored change to client or archived evidence with no completed ticket (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:75; factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py:162).

The archived-review display has no defined read representation. The board currently obtains task review status from `reviews/selected.json` and a valid selected generation; simply moving fixed lens files into an archive cannot make such a task display as reviewed (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:79; factory/scripts/forge_cli/board.py:97; docs/QUALITY.md:171).

The upgrade skill is installed as a setup-pinned copy, while the spec describes changing its runbook. It does not state how an already-installed old copy learns the new branch, parking, and commit procedure before it directs the first upgrade; the existing runbook still expects an uncommitted diff and manual commit (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:87; setup:66; install/claude/knacklabs-upgrade-project/SKILL.md:81).

The acceptance fixtures name two historical commits and an unspecified Lean-era commit, but do not name a pre-rename commit or test the required pre-rename refusal and usable intermediate-upgrade advice. That boundary remains unproved by the stated end-to-end fixtures (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:94; docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:104).
contradictions: The title and promised behavior say one step from any client version, but the spec refuses pre-rename clients and requires an intermediate upgrade with an older harness first (docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:3; docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:27).
resolutions: Exact route for pre-rename clients: this story tags the last .agents-migrating harness commit `forge-legacy-upgrade`; the refusal tells the developer to check it out in a separate worktree, run its upgrade, then this one (Behaviour: Scope).
The vendored commit must be an ancestor of the harness HEAD; unknown, unrelated or newer commits are refused, so no downgrade (Behaviour: Before anything is written; AC3).
Fail closed: a listed worktree that cannot be read (missing folder or unreadable state) is refused by name with `git worktree prune` suggested (Behaviour; AC4).
Any plan in plans/active/ whose roadmap item is not done counts as work in progress, approved or not, so a plan awaiting approval is never stranded (Behaviour; AC4).

Parking is refused while another worktree holds the story's pointer or stage (remove those worktrees first); in the target it archives state, clears a pointer at the story, and resets the roadmap item (Behaviour: Parking; AC5).
Parking also archives the story's plan record (plan-meta) and clears its run pointer, so a new plan can be saved; AC5 tests that replanning is reachable.

The archive table is narrowed to what actually breaks current readers: fixed per-lens review files and the root decomposition/tests/verify singletons; grill records stay in place (Behaviour step 2; AC8).
Unshipped client files inside factory/, constitution/ or harness/ (except client skills) are refused by name before any write, so client code is never frozen into the gate manifest (Behaviour; AC6).

The lock boundary is stated: acquiring upgrade's own git-local lock is not a repository write; preflight runs under it; a refusal changes no repository file, branch or git-local state (Behaviour: Before anything is written).
The health step now includes `forge doctor --fast` and a board data load before the commit (Behaviour step 4).

Ticket-check provenance: the upgrade commit carries a Forge-Upgrade trailer, and the exemption applies only when every change is harness-owned, the manifest, an exact (100%) rename of an archive-table path into .factory/archive/pre-*/, or one of Forge's own ignore blocks; AC9 tests a hand-made change is not exempt (Behaviour: After the upgrade).
Archived-review display is defined: a task with no selected review but archived review files shows as 'reviewed before upgrade' on the board (Behaviour: Archived reviews; AC8).

Upgrade prints its own next steps, so an older installed skill copy still leads to the right result; forge doctor warns when the installed skill differs from the harness copy (Behaviour: The upgrade skill).
Acceptance fixtures now name 47516c55 as the Lean-era commit and add a pre-rename fixture (before 2ebba90d) that must be refused with the legacy instructions (AC1, AC2).
Title and scope now say any factory-era client (vendored after the 2026-07-24 rename); pre-rename clients take one older step first (Title; Behaviour: Scope).
